sigma_analysis_results.rule_title: Files With System Process Name In Unsuspected Locations
sigma_analysis_results.rule_description:
Detects the creation of an executable with a system process name in folders other than the system ones (System32, SysWOW64, etc.).
It is highly recommended to perform an initial baseline before using this rule in production.
sigma_analysis_results.rule_author: Sander Wiebing, Tim Shelton, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

attributes.magic: PE32+ executable (GUI) x86-64, for MS Windows

crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The binary is a legitimate instance of the Windows Service Host process (svchost.exe). Its functionality is dedicated to loading and managing Windows services from DLL files. It reads service configurations from standard registry locations like 'HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services' and 'HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Svchost', loads the specified 'ServiceDll' via LoadLibraryExW, and executes its 'ServiceMain' function. The presence of functions like SvcHostMain, GetServiceMainFunctions, and ServiceStarter, along with a string 'Host Process for Windows Services', confirms its identity. No malicious behavior was observed.
